title: Getting things done
cando: say what you have and haven’t done, and deal with offices, forms and repairs

about.text: In this lesson you get things done. You renew a card, fill in a form and report a fault in your home. You also say what you have and haven't done, and you cancel an appointment.
goals: Ask for things at a counter: I'd like to renew my licence, please.
Say what is done and not done: I've already signed it. Not yet.
Say why with so that: Can you post it, so that I don't have to come back?
Read a counter notice and fill in a repair form.
Report a fault, book a repair and write a message to cancel.

chapters.title: At the counter
chapters.text:
In this lesson you get things done: cards, forms and repairs.
First, you listen to Samir. He is at a counter in a city office. He wants to renew his driving licence.
The assistant asks: Have you filled in the form? Samir says: Yes, I've already filled it in.
Then she asks: Have you signed it yet? Samir says: Not yet. Sorry!
Listen for the short v in I've. It is quiet, but it is important.

chapters.title: Done, not done, and why
chapters.text:
There are two grammar points in this lesson.
One. To say something is done, use have or has and a past form. I've posted the letter. She's signed the form.
Already means it is done, maybe sooner than you think. I've already printed it.
Yet is for questions and for not. Have you signed it yet? No, not yet.
Still means it is not done, and it is late. I still haven't received my card.
With a past time, like yesterday, use the past: I posted it yesterday.
Two. To say why, use so that. Write clearly, so that we can read it.

chapters.title: A notice and a form
chapters.text:
Next, you read a notice at a counter. It tells you what to do before you join the queue.
Then you read a repair form. Read every instruction.
Block capitals are big letters, like this: A, B, C. Tick one box means one box only.
Then you fill in the form. You also write a message to cancel an appointment.

chapters.title: Three errands
chapters.text:
In the task, it is your day off, and you have three errands.
First, you renew your library card at a counter.
Then you phone the housing office about a fault in your flat. The heating doesn't work.
Say what you have already tried. Then book a time for the repair.
Say why with so that: The morning, please, so that I can go to work after.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a story or an article about getting things done.
Read it once for the main idea. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You need to renew a card. How do you do it?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many things are online now. But sometimes you still have to go to a counter, with a form and your documents.

conversation.title: At the counter
conversation.setting: Samir is a delivery driver. His driving licence runs out this month. He is at the City Service Centre, and now it is his turn at Counter 4.
lines: Next, please! Sorry about the long queue. How can I help?
Hi. I'd like to renew my driving licence, please.
OK. Have you filled in the application form?
Yes, I've already filled it in. Here you are.
Thanks. Have you signed it yet?
Oh, not yet. Sorry! Where do I sign?
Here, at the bottom. Have you got a document with your address on it?
Yes. I've printed a letter from my bank, and here's a photocopy of my old licence.
Great. Please write your phone number here too, so that we can call you.
OK. Can you post the new licence to me, so that I don't have to come back? I work long days.
Yes, of course. You'll receive it in about ten days.
And what if it still hasn't arrived after two weeks?
Then call us, and give this reference number. Anything else?
No, that's everything. Thanks for your help!

items.example: Take your form to Counter 4.

items.meaning: A line of people who are waiting for something.
items.example: The queue at the post office was very long today.

items.meaning: To get a new card or licence when the old one runs out.
items.example: I have to renew my passport this year.

items.meaning: To go to a place and get something that is waiting for you.
items.example: You can collect your new card from the counter on Monday.

items.meaning: To send a letter or a parcel. You put it in a red box in the street, or take it to a counter.
items.example: I posted the letters this morning.

items.meaning: To get something that someone sends or gives you.

items.meaning: To make a paper copy of something on a computer.

items.meaning: To give or send a form to an office.

items.meaning: A form you fill in to ask for something, like a job or a licence.

items.meaning: An important paper, like a passport, a letter from a bank or a contract.

items.meaning: A paper that looks exactly like another paper. A machine makes it.

items.meaning: A small paper square on a letter. It shows you have paid to send the letter.

items.meaning: An official card or paper. It says you can do something, like drive a car.

sound.title: I've, she's and haven't
sound.explain: In speech, have is short: I've, you've, we've. Has is short too: she's, he's. So listen for the small v in I've: I've signed it. Haven't and not yet are strong and clear. Listen, then say each group.
groups: I haven't · she hasn't · not yet

sayIt.instructions: Say Samir's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Can you hear the v in I've?
lines: Hi. I'd like to renew my driving licence, please.
Yes, I've already filled it in. Here you are.
Oh, not yet. Sorry! Where do I sign?
And what if it still hasn't arrived after two weeks?

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Four talk about what is done or not done. The last one says why.
examples: Have you filled in the application form?
Yes, I've already filled it in.
And what if it still hasn't arrived after two weeks?
Please write your phone number here too, so that we can call you.
spot.question: Which words say that something is done? Where do already, yet and still go? What does so that tell you?
spot.answer: Have or has + a past form: I've filled it in. Already goes in the middle, before the past form. Yet goes at the end of a question or a not sentence. Still goes before hasn't or haven't. So that says why: so that we can call you.

rules.title: Have you done it yet? already, yet, still
rule: have or has + a past form: I've filled in the form. She's posted the letter.
Some verbs change: do – done, send – sent, write – written, bring – brought.
already, in the middle: I've already printed it. It is done, maybe early.
yet, at the end of a question or a not sentence: Have you signed it yet? I haven't signed it yet.
still, before haven't or hasn't: I still haven't received my card. It's late!
rules.mistake: Not: I've posted it yesterday. Say: I posted it yesterday. With a past time, use the past.

rules.title: so that: saying why
rule: so that + a sentence says why: I'm here so that I can renew my card.
It often has can: Write in block capitals, so that we can read it.
It says what you want to happen: Post it today, so that it arrives on Monday.
so alone is different. It says what happened: The office was closed, so I went home.
Why? — So that I don't have to come back.
rules.mistake: Not: I'm here so that renew my card. Say: I'm here so that I can renew my card.

practice.q: I've ___ the form. Here it is.
practice.why: have + a past form: I've filled in.
She takes has: she has posted.

practice.q: I haven't signed it ___ . I'll do it now.
practice.why: Yet goes at the end of a not sentence.

practice.q: I've ___ printed it. Look, here it is.
It's two weeks now, and I ___ haven't received my card.
practice.why: Still + haven't: it is not done, and it's late.
Last Monday is a past time, so use the past.

practice.q: Have you ___ the email to the office?
Write in block capitals ___ we can read your name.
practice.why: So that says why: so that we can read it.

practice.q: The office was closed, ___ I went home.
I've brought a photocopy, so that you ___ keep it.
practice.why: So that + a sentence, often with can.

yourTurn.prompt: It's Friday afternoon. Look at your list of jobs for the week. Write four or five sentences: what you have already done, what you haven't done yet, and why you need to do it.
yourTurn.model: I've already posted the letters to the bank. I've renewed my library card too. I haven't printed the train tickets yet. I still haven't booked an appointment with the dentist. I need to phone the dentist on Monday, so that I can get an early appointment.

text.title: A counter notice and a repair request form
text.body:
PRACTICE NOTICE: for English practice only.

CITY SERVICE CENTRE
COUNTER 4: RENEWALS AND APPLICATIONS
Open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm. Closed 1 pm to 2 pm.

BEFORE YOU JOIN THE QUEUE
Fill in your form and sign it.
Bring one document with your name and address.
Have your reference number ready.

NOT AT THIS COUNTER
Lost cards: go to Counter 6.
Payments: go to Counter 2.

Your new card or licence comes by post in 10 days.
Can't come to your appointment? Please cancel by 4 pm the day before, so that someone else can have it.

- - - - - - - -

PRACTICE FORM: this company does not exist.

BROOKMEAD HOMES: REPAIR REQUEST
Section A. Please write in BLOCK CAPITALS.
Surname: __________   First name: __________
Address and postcode: __________
Phone: __________

Section B. What is the problem? Tick ONE box.
☐ Heating   ☐ Water   ☐ Electrics   ☐ Door or window
Is it urgent? For example: no heating in winter, a big leak, or a door that doesn't lock.
☐ Yes   ☐ No
Describe the fault: __________

Signature: __________   Date: __________
We send back forms with no signature. We reply in 5 working days.

gist.a: It tells people what to do at Counter 4.
wrong: It tells people how to fix a leak.
It is an advert for a new card.
gist.why: The notice says: Counter 4: renewals and applications. Before you join the queue …

gist.a: asking for a repair in your home
gist.why: The form says: Brookmead Homes: repair request.

detail.q: You have lost your card. Where do you go?
detail.why: The notice says: Lost cards: go to Counter 6.

detail.q: Your appointment is on Thursday. When is the last time to cancel it?
detail.why: The notice says: Please cancel by 4 pm the day before.

detail.q: How many boxes do you tick for the problem in Section B?
detail.why: The form says: Tick ONE box.

detail.q: What happens if you forget to sign the form?
detail.a: They send it back to you.
wrong: They do the repair in 5 days.
detail.why: The form says: We send back forms with no signature.

items.meaning: A piece of paper on a wall or a door. It gives people information or rules.
items.example: Read the notice before you join the queue.

items.meaning: One part of a form, a document or a book.
items.example: Please fill in Section A in block capitals.

items.meaning: To make a small mark (✓) in a box, to choose an answer.
items.example: Tick one box only.

items.meaning: Big letters that are not joined, LIKE THIS.
items.example: Please write your name in block capitals.

items.meaning: Your name, written by you in your own way, to show you agree.
items.example: The form needs your signature and the date.

items.meaning: Work to make something that is broken good again.
items.example: The repair to the heating took two hours.

items.meaning: A small hole or crack. Water or gas comes out of it.
items.example: There's a leak under the kitchen sink.

items.meaning: Broken parts or marks on something after a problem, like a leak or an accident.
items.example: The leak did a lot of damage to the floor.

items.meaning: Something wrong with a machine, so it doesn't work well.
items.example: There's a fault with the lift.

items.meaning: It needs help now. It can't wait.
items.example: The leak is urgent. Water is going everywhere.

items.meaning: To say that a plan or an appointment is not going to happen.
items.example: I need to cancel my appointment on Friday.

model.title: A form, and a message to cancel
model.body:
PRACTICE FORM, FILLED IN
REPAIR REQUEST: BROOKMEAD HOMES
Section A. Surname: NOWAK   First name: TOMASZ
Address and postcode: FLAT 6, 22 HILL STREET, KELLBRIDGE KB4 7QX
Phone: 07700 900 358
Section B. ✓ Door or window   Is it urgent? ✓ No
Describe the fault: The kitchen window doesn't close. It started last week. There's no damage, but the kitchen is cold at night. I've already tried the window key, but it doesn't turn.

write.task: Fill in the repair form for a fault in your home. It can be real or made up. Then write a short message to cancel the repair appointment, and ask for a new day.
checklist: I wrote my name in block capitals, and I ticked one box.
I described the fault: what happens, when it started, and what I've already tried.
My message says which appointment, and why I have to cancel it.
I signed the form, and I asked for a new day in my message.

card.title: Three errands
card.situation: It's your day off, and you have three things to do. Your library card runs out this week. The heating in your flat doesn't work. And you need a time for the repair.
card.goal: Renew your card at the library counter. Then phone the housing office. Report the fault, and book a repair appointment at a good time for you.

phrases: I'd like to renew my library card, please.
I've already filled in the form. / Not yet, sorry.
I'd like to report a fault. My heating doesn't work.
I've already switched it off and on again.
The morning, please, so that I can go to work after.
Tuesday, 8 to 10. What's the reference number?
prepare.notes: Make notes for each errand: what you want, what you have already done, and one question. Write one sentence with so that.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is the assistant at the library counter, then the person on the phone at the housing office. Do your errands. Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You are two people. First, you are an assistant at a library counter. I want to renew my card. Ask me if I have filled in the form. Then you are a person on the phone at a housing office. I report a fault. Ask me what I have already tried, and book a repair appointment with me. Use simple English.

model.title: The card and the repair
lines: Next, please. How can I help?
Hi. I'd like to renew my library card, please.
Have you filled in the form yet?
Yes, I've already filled it in and signed it. Here you are.
Thank you. That's done. Here's your new card.
Brookmead Homes, repairs. How can I help?
Hello. I'd like to report a fault. My heating doesn't work.
I'm sorry to hear that. Have you switched it off and on again?
Yes, I've already done that. It still doesn't work, and the flat is very cold.
OK, that's urgent. We can come on Tuesday, in the morning or the afternoon.
The morning, please, so that I can go to work after.
Fine. Tuesday, between 8 and 10. Your reference number is BH-5902.
compare: Did you say what you wanted: I'd like to renew …, I'd like to report …?
Did you answer Have you …? with I've already … or Not yet?
Did you say why with so that?
Did you say the day, the time and the reference number back to check them?

canDo: I can ask for what I need at a counter.
I can say what I have and haven't done, with already, yet and still.
I can say why with so that.
I can read a counter notice and fill in a repair form.
I can report a fault, book a repair and write a message to cancel it.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Where is the person? What do they need to get done?
reading.talk: Did the person in the story get everything done? What have you done this week? What haven't you done yet? Write three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: Have you posted the letter ___ ? — No, not yet.
quiz.why: Yet goes at the end of a question.

quiz.q: I've ___ filled in the form. Here it is.
She ___ received her new card yet.
quiz.why: She + hasn't, with yet at the end.
Yesterday is a past time, so use the past.

quiz.q: Write clearly, ___ we can read it.
quiz.why: So that says why: so that we can read it.

quiz.q: There's water on the floor under the sink. There's a ___ .
quiz.why: A leak: water comes out of a small hole.

quiz.q: You write your name LIKE THIS. These letters are ___ .
quiz.why: Block capitals are big letters that are not joined.

quiz.q: Would you like ___ come to lunch on Sunday?
quiz.why: Would you like to + a verb invites someone.

quiz.q: ___ push the door. Pull it towards you.
quiz.why: Don't + a verb says what not to do.

quiz.q: You ___ wear a suit. Jeans are fine.
quiz.why: Jeans are fine, so a suit is not necessary.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the counter conversation in pairs. Then change what they renew: a library card, a bus pass, a parking permit. Listen for the short v in I've.
Day 2: a to-do list game. Each learner writes five errands and ticks three. A partner asks Have you … yet? and they answer with already, not yet or still. Then each learner says why with so that.
Day 3: the task. You are the library assistant, then the repairs office on the phone. Each learner renews a card, reports a fault and books a repair time.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and read two cancel messages aloud.
